answer: In the observational STAR-RA study of routine care rheumatoid arthritis patients initiating tofacitinib versus TNF inhibitors, researchers found no evidence of an increased risk of cardiovascular outcomes overall; however, in patients with rheumatoid arthritis who had cardiovascular risk factors, tofacitinib was associated with an increased, though statistically non-significant, risk of cardiovascular outcomes. In the randomized, open-label ORAL Surveillance trial comparing tofacitinib (5 mg or 10 mg twice daily) to TNF inhibitors in rheumatoid arthritis patients aged 50 or older with at least one cardiovascular risk factor, the risks of adjudicated MACE and cancers were higher with tofacitinib and failed to meet non-inferiority criteria. In its September 1, 2021 Drug Safety Communication, the FDA required updated warnings regarding an increased risk of serious heart-related events, cancer, blood clots, and death for tofacitinib and other Janus kinase inhibitors based on its review of the randomized safety clinical trial in patients with rheumatoid arthritis. The prescribing information for tofacitinib (dated November 10, 2026) continues to warn of major adverse cardiovascular events and mortality, reporting higher rates of MACE and all-cause mortality compared with TNF inhibitors in rheumatoid arthritis patients aged 50 and older with cardiovascular risk factors. Although the observational STAR-RA study did not identify an overall cardiovascular risk elevation in routine care rheumatoid arthritis patients, its findings do not establish that the FDA withdrew its warnings, as the FDA's September 1, 2021 action was based on the randomized ORAL Surveillance trial, and warnings for MACE and mortality remain active in the November 10, 2026 indexed label.
